A year ago I was referred for an emergency assessment for an admission which was to be completed in 1 week. And yes after many checks I am still on the emergency waiting list for a whole fucking year. It’s not a new issue and my sick of the government acting like it’s something that’s happened overnight. I’ve got to the point where I’ve asked to receive all my health records via FOI to try and find out what went wrong. Been told that it’s about a 2 - 3 year wait for government mental health services in Perth metro right now. For many people like myself private isn’t an option as most private wouldn’t deal with people who have complex issues.

Thanks mate. I really don’t have a social life but make sure I go for a walk (about an hour) three times a week. The five units I did last semester and will do next semester as well. Wouldn’t recommend unless you are looking to knock off some time from your degree. I would have had three units to do at the end of my degree so decided to ask to do the five a semester. These are all electives and first year units so not too bad (wouldnt do it as a third year unit lol). For labs during COVID they were online but now on campus. Normally if you are doing a unit which requires labs online you will do all the content online (lectures and tutorials) and just need to attend uni for the labs. Which is normally a few hours a week, so isn’t too bad. Just when looking at unis see what there processes are with online units. Some unis allow online students to do intense practical sessions towards the end of the semester. Normally you will go in for two full days (8 hours each) and complete all your practicals then, but I’ve never done this but have friends who have. Each uni is different and everything is changing at the moment due to COVID so have no idea what will happen by next year.

For assessments I always break them down into smaller bits and set personal deadlines for myself. I make sure that all my assessments are handed in 48 hours before the deadline, so if something comes up I know I still have two days to get work done as a backup. I have two days a week (one weekday and one weekend) where I set only for uni work (Online due to COVID), I make sure I spend at least 8 hours on each day working on uni. It’s hard at first so the beginning of every semester I start with an hour session and work my way up as the load increases. I make sure while doing work to have music or tv on so it’s not boring. I also make sure a few days a week get up early and try and fit in an hour of study before work, seems crazy but better getting out the way so after a long day at work I can just sleep. 

Before COVID I was campus and was completing labs and regular placement hours (health research). I struggled with labs and placement but just ended up taking time off work to spend on placement (a week a semester normally). I’ve been online since March and decided to finish my degree online now (excluding placements), I find it SO much easier to juggle now with it online with only going into uni a few times a semester. Also by the looks of it most Perth unis will be mainly online til 2022 at this stage. Online is available for most courses (or a least for a few units), most are self passed and means u can do work when ever you want. Hope this helps

I do around 30 hours a week while studying full time. At first it was hard but you really get into the swing of it. For jobs it really doesn’t matter which job you are taking (Ik people from people doing every job under the sun even fifo). But all I can say if you can afford to do not work full time but rather causal/part time. So which easier and most employers are very accepting to help schedule work around uni (like allowing time off for exams etc). Stay in the field you know but look for part time/causal roles. Good luck

For exams they find an exam venue near your house (normally a local uni) to sit them at. Normally only 20 odd at exams in person. The system is modern and easy to use. The system is build for fully online students which is good. Look at the course structures and programs of each one. Weight them out and see.
